After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, the conclusion remains SUPPORTED. 

H1 (one-time items/restructuring): While evidence shows that Alphabet-level activities included employee severance and office space charges during 2025 (E13, E14), there is no evidence that these items were excluded from the reported operating margin or that they materially distorted the 32% operating margin figure reported in the 10-K for fiscal year 2025. The operating margin presented in E5 appears to be the standard GAAP operating margin inclusive of all such charges.

H2 (non-GAAP adjustments): The evidence shows that Alphabet uses non-GAAP metrics for constant currency revenues (E15, E16), but there is no evidence of a non-GAAP or adjusted operating margin. The 32% operating margin reported in E5 for fiscal year 2025 appears to be the standard GAAP operating margin calculation (operating income divided by revenues).

H3 (restatements): No evidence was found of any restatements, corrections, or amendments to the fiscal year 2025 operating margin figures.

The claim that Alphabet's operating margin for fiscal year 2025 exceeded 30% is directly supported by E5, which shows a 32% operating margin for the year ended December 31, 2025. Since 32% > 30%, the claim is supported.
